body:
> so they can be test with navigation helpers

Test by whom? It's not clear to me that message must be equal to digest. The digest should be additional information.
author: eps1lon

body:
> > so they can be test with navigation helpers
> 
> Test by whom? It's not clear to me that message must be equal to digest. The digest should be additional information.

More like a aligning the presentation side for consumer side (or in application). When users receive an error they might not always check the `error.digest` or they could copy the error.message into a new error. This could lost the context of the `digest`. Having a unique error message for notFound/forbidden/unauthorized errors will still be helpful to identify the actual error if users accidentally display or consume the `message` somewhere in their system
author: huozhi

body: But we shouldn't encourage just consuming the message. That's not leading our users to success. The digest is important to consider.
author: eps1lon

body: Yea true but still if in some case it's erroring in error dialog, it's also easy for us to know which API is throwing that and help for investigation. I don't see a reason why we shouldn't change it tho
author: huozhi

body:
>  I don't see a reason why we shouldn't change it tho

Because it looks weird and we don't equate digest with the message in other cases.

> Yea true but still if in some case it's erroring in error dialog

That would be a bug. Please share a repro. If it's not a bug, we should revert this PR since this is a bad message format to surface to the user.
author: eps1lon

body:
It's already displaying the internal error code, reverting it back without status didn't make it better.
The solution is to hide the internal case for the cases when they're surfacing to dialog which is addressed in https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/73100

body:
> One struct seems to be trivially used in a trait which requires it to be a Vc so I left it with a comment. @bgw perhaps we can set up some lint + disabling comment for all the cases in this doc?

Unfortunately, we still need to enforce that it uses `ResolvedVc` because if we don't, we can't know for certain that there isn't some callsite of that type *somewhere* (now or in the future) that uses it with an unresolved `Vc`.

We must update all implementations of the trait as well, which is why some of these migrations are hard.

Because `Vc` and `ResolvedVc` share the same in-memory representation (guaranteed via `#[repr(transparent)]`), we can create a safe zero-cost transmute wrapper function that can convert `Vec<ResolvedVc<T>>` back to `Vec<Vc<T>>` using [`Vec::from_raw_parts`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.from_raw_parts). That won't work for most other collections, but it can for `Vec` since it provides the `from_raw_parts` API.

We could probably also provide a faster-but-still-safe API for doing an in-place (still `O(n)` as we need to check and possibly resolve each item) conversion of `Vec<Vc<T>>` to `Vec<ResolvedVc<T>>`.

body: @cramforce For the same reason you want it for css and js bundles. Because if the file content changes then you'll get a 404. For example, `import logo from './logo.png'`, creates a file `/_next/static/media/logo.97e00142.jpg`. Then `` optimizes it using ``. If we don't add the `dpl` then it could suffer from version skew when the content of the logo changes. I pushed a change in [0aa4022](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/73184/commits/0aa4022680332da1f0f35875153155dc8f1b5f5c) to narrow this down.

Sounds like we should remove `packages/next-codemod/transforms/revalidate-to-expire.ts`? 

Or rather they need to be limited to a version range and new rename codemods from `expireTag` to `unstable_expireTag` are needed. Though that's a pretty small target audience so probably not worth it. Search and replace should be good enough.

body: Thanks so much for adding support so quickly! I noticed that, while it now correctly handles `notFound()` by falling back to the not-found page, the log outputs `unhandledRejection: Error: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` — is this intended?
author: timomeh

body:
> Thanks so much for adding support so quickly! I noticed that, while it now correctly handles `notFound()` by falling back to the not-found page, the log outputs `unhandledRejection: Error: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` — is this intended?

@timomeh What would be a repro for that? I don't see an unhandled rejection when running our [test fixture](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/2b765475303512c9d8958908cf72e8b939dbaff5/test/e2e/app-dir/use-cache/app/not-found/page.tsx).
author: unstubbable

body:
@unstubbable I updated my reproduction of the original issue: https://github.com/timomeh/next-canaray24-not-found-issue

1. `npm run dev`
2. Open localhost:3000
3. Click on `💥 Example with 'use cache'` (path `/example-with-cache`)
4. It will render the not found page, but the dev server logs the following:

```
 ✓ Compiled /example-with-cache in 209ms (630 modules)
Error: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404
    at notFound (app/example-with-cache/page.tsx:6:10)
  4 |   'use cache'
  5 |
> 6 |   notFound()
    |          ^
  7 |
  8 |   return (
  9 |     <div> {
  environmentName: 'Cache',
  digest: ''
}
 ⨯ app/example-with-cache/page.tsx (6:11) @ notFound
 ⨯ unhandledRejection: Error: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404
    at notFound (app/example-with-cache/page.tsx:6:10)
```
author: timomeh

body: @timomeh Thank you. The culprit that masked the error was a suspense boundary in the root layout of our test fixture. I've addressed the issue in #73607.

> only thing I think we maybe should do still is leave comments in the locations we use cloneResponse to indicate why we aren't just calling .clone(). We should also remind our future selves to remove this code once we no longer support a version that has the underlying bug if we can ever pinpoint what it is

This has already been pinpointed and several community members have attempted to flag this down both in Pro support chats on Vercel and on discussions in this repository.  @ tagging Vercel members here on GitHub seems to yield no results.

It presents itself in a recent release of Node 20.17.

See #69635

body:
Hey @JamBalaya56562! 👋🏼  

Since v15 is now the latest stable version and using React 19 canary, you'll get a warning when using `useFormState`. We mention the hook update in our docs ([here](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/upgrading/version-15#react-19)). 

I'll close your PR because the stable version React 19 is coming soon (👀), so we don't have to duplicate the work. We'll also need to update any other mentions of `useFormState` to `useActionState`.

body:
Excellent work! 👏 This feature is truly needed by the community.

I actively use intercepted routes in production applications and constantly encounter situations where I need to conditionally disable interception. This is especially critical for:

- Dashboard interfaces - when you need to open a resource in a modal window for quick viewing, but navigate to a full page for editing
- E-commerce catalogs - quick product preview in overlay, but full page for detailed examination
- Admin panels - where UX requires different behavior for different actions

Currently, we have to use workarounds through window.location.href or history.pushState , which breaks SPA navigation and hurts performance.

Key advantages of this PR:

- ✅ Backward compatibility (opt-in via intercept={false} )
- ✅ Covered with tests
- ✅ Documentation added
- ✅ Solves real developer problems (#49146, #51648, #70886)

This isn't just a "nice to have" feature - it's a solution to an architectural problem that everyone who seriously uses intercepted routes encounters.

Request: Could we expedite the review and merge? The community has been waiting for this functionality for several years. 🙏

body:
Thank you @okisdev. 

The docs in the Next.js repo reflect the latest **canary** version where the file path was changed, hence the updated links. 

If you access the links from the **stable** version, it'll take you to the old URL path, which is still valid for that version. And if you access the links from the **canary**, it'll take you to the new URL path. 

It's a little confusing, but what this means is that we don't have to change back the links as they are working as expected for their respective versions. 

Have you come across any 404s while navigating the docs?
author: delbaoliveira

body:
Hi @delbaoliveira. Thanks for reaching back.

Let's do a simple validation for the diff in this PR.

![CleanShot 2024-12-03 at 20 17 14@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43d1bc72-4db5-4caa-88bf-eae544e8911c)

file `errors/built-in-css-disabled.mdx` points to https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/built-in-css-disabled, but if you go to this page at **Useful Links** Section, the **Custom webpack config docs** will redirect to a 404 pages.

![CleanShot 2024-12-03 at 20 19 34@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6693d52-3916-4fa4-8e41-175bb664dd45)

Also, if you go to

- https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/deprecated-target-config
- https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/empty-configuration
- ...

They are facing the same issue.

Can you reproduce this from your perspective?
author: okisdev

body:
I see, thank you. 

The error messages are outside docs "versioning" which would explain why the links are 404. 

Since we can't change the links as this would break the version of the canary docs ([link validation is failing for this PR](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/actions/runs/12131299255/job/33823185067?pr=73400)), a quick fix would be to have temporary redirects in place, but this can quickly get messy as pages move around.

A better, long-term solution would be to improve the flow between canary and stable docs. I've talked to my team about it, and we have a solution. 

I'll be closing this PR and work on that in the next few days, but appreciate you raising this as it helped us talk through it 🙏🏼

body:
> I'm not sure if this is the same capabilities—the Remote MDX example is using raw Markdown text, whereas my example is importing a markdown file as a Component. If we fetched MDX text, how would we pa

With this part "If we fetched MDX text, how would we pa", I guess you mean "how would we parse and compile the MDX"

Maybe `@next/mdx` won't completely take over all capabilities of `next-mdx-remote`, but maybe your next comment also has a suggestion of how to deal with that:

> Oh I guess we have this section → [nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/configuring/mdx#deep-dive-how-do-you-transform-markdown-into-html](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/configuring/mdx#deep-dive-how-do-you-transform-markdown-into-html)

That's a good point, we could potentially suggest that.

> Maybe we just remove this line from the Remote MDX section → " content stored in a separate local folder"?

In case you think there's a high value of keeping the "Remote MDX" section, this would also be a possibility:

Eg. remove the parts about local files, which overlap with `@next/mdx` capabilities with `await import()`.

Maybe also add more language about this being an "alternative" and more emphasis that it's "third party". Could also be moved further down in the docs.

> `<MDXRemote source={markdown} />`

This looks suspicious. `markdown` is a string. Is the source markdown or MDX? Usually this is inferred from the file name, defaulting to MDX. But no file name is given here and the variable is named `markdown`.

Adding here as well that updating the docs here doesn’t fix the issue in that ticket. The issue with that ticket is Next 15 now adds a hash to the URL that is undocumented and will cause things like Google Search Console to no longer find sitemaps that were previously there in Next 14.

While this change does fix that both local and prod sitemap URLs are the same, it doesn’t address the hash issue.

body: You changed the vendored version of React we use in the App Router. It's automatically updated with the latest `canary` not latest stable (i.e. `latest`).
author: eps1lon

body:
@eps1lon is it planned to go back to non-canary versions of `react` and `react-dom` in the user's / project's `package.json` file?

Eg. usage of `react@19.0.0` and `react-dom@19.0.0` in `<project root>/package.json`, even though Next.js uses a different canary version internally?

The reason I ask is that automated npm package upgraders like Renovate bot and Dependabot will automatically bump the versions of `next`, `react` and `react-dom` in an indiscriminate way - they will just bump to the latest versions. These upgrades often cause mismatches between the Next.js-internal versions of `react`/`react-dom` and the project's `package.json` versions of `react`/`react-dom`, causing build failures. This has happened to us at least 10 times in our projects in the last months/years. 

Why not just disable the automated upgrades for `react`/`react-dom`? Because that will still fail over time, as newly auto-upgraded versions of Next.js rely internally on new `react`/`react-dom` versions, causing a mismatch with the stale versions from the time of disabling.

I have come up with a workaround for this in the interim - using GitHub Actions workflows and a shell script to fix the version numbers after the bots upgrade to mismatching `react`/`react-dom` in `package.json`:

- https://github.com/karlhorky/next-js-tricks?tab=readme-ov-file#github-actions-automated-upgrades-to-nextjs-internal-react-versions

But ideally there would be a more bulletproof way to allow these upgrader bots to upgrade to the latest stable versions of all packages (eg. as it was before Next.js started requiring canary versions of `react`/`react-dom` in the project `package.json`).

Alternative: Next.js could stop requiring `react`/`react-dom` in the project `package.json` and only use its internal versions (maybe also using `peerDependencies` in some way)
author: karlhorky

body:
> is it planned to go back to non-canary versions of react and react-dom in the user's / project's package.json file?

Yes.

If Renovate is doing upgrades that create conflicting peer dependencies, I'd file that against their repo.

The version of React in `peerDependencies` is for Pages router so we can't just drop it.

> These upgrades often cause mismatches between the Next.js-internal versions of react/react-dom and the project's package.json versions of react/react-dom, causing build failures. 

I don't see how this would be frequent. The latest version of Next.js was always immediately supporting the latest version of React so there should rarely be a long period of mismatch.

> Can you sourcemap these instead to empty function names so that it's consistent with terminals and debuggers? We should just display no function name as `at ${location}`.

They had no function name before. The problem is that browser "infer" a name when there is non. That's why I did give them a name to avoid that. `eval()` isn't even a function, it's more a "source", which I can't give a name. `anonymous` is the fallback name when the browser can't infer a better name.

body:
> @JamBalaya56562 These are still not using `.env.example` (starting with a `.`)

I'm sorry but I'm not sure what you mean.

By the way, I will tell you why the dotfiles aren't made by `create-next-app`.

You can create `.env.example` correctly in local [create-next-app folder](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/packages/create-next-app).
However, you can't do that with `dist/index.ts` after build because of [@vercel/ncc](https://github.com/vercel/ncc/tree/main) compile.
[@vercel/ncc](https://github.com/vercel/ncc/tree/main) doesn't output dotfiles to `dist` folder.

That's why `.gitignore` is replaced with [`gitignore`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/create-next-app/templates/app/js/gitignore).
